summary.name: On-call doesn't have to suck
summary.one_liner: A Medium essay by Cindy Sridharan (copyconstruct) arguing that on-call burden is a reflection of engineering culture, system design and prioritization rather than an unavoidable part of the job.
use_cases: Making the case for a healthier on-call rotation on a team
Deciding how developers should share on-call duties with SREs
Preparing a talk or discussion on engineering culture and reliability
summary.what_it_does: The essay is an opinion piece rather than a tool. It describes the author's experience being on-call as a developer and argues that on-call is a reflection of engineering skill, monitoring, alerting and culture. It lists common causes of bad on-call, such as noisy or non-actionable alerts, bad deploys, missing runbooks and no blameless postmortems. It argues that developers owning their services should receive training and that on-call should be compensated more formally. It ends by urging engineers to build reliability into systems from the start and to drive bottom-up cultural change.
notable: Lists concrete causes of bad on-call, from noisy alerts to unfollowed postmortem action items
Argues on-call quality reflects engineering culture and prioritization
Calls for developer on-call training and formal on-call compensation
caveats: Opinion essay, not a product; no software features or pricing are described
Recommendations are general and not tied to specific tools or data
